title: Async handlers accept and forward the request CancellationToken
statement: A minimal API handler that awaits I/O declares a `CancellationToken cancellationToken` parameter (minimal APIs bind it to the request-aborted token automatically) and passes that same token into every async call it makes, instead of `default`/`CancellationToken.None`.
rationale: ASP.NET Core cancels the bound token when the client disconnects or the request times out. A handler that drops the token keeps doing work — file reads, review agent calls, sensor scans — for a caller that already left, wasting the exact review-agent tokens and wall-clock the rest of this codebase is careful to account for.

good.caption: Bound CancellationToken forwarded into the async call.

bad.caption: Token accepted but replaced with CancellationToken.None on the call that matters.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in the GuidelineImpact endpoint's token propagation.
